terms.gloss: be available, be at hand, be in store
terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation, intransitive; to whom, the dative
evidence: Caes. BG 1.16.2: nē pābulī quidem satis magna cōpia suppetēbat
Cic. Fam. 15.13.2: mihi ad remūnerandum nihil suppetat praeter voluntātem
terms.comment: Latin says “X is available” with a verb: suppetit, it is there to be had.

terms.gloss: be ready to hand; be obvious
evidence: Gell. 2.29.20: hoc erit tibi argūmentum semper in prōmptū situm

terms.grammar: to whom, the dative; of what, the genitive
evidence: Ter. Ph. 113: sibi ut ejus faciat cōpiam

phrases.latin: hoc erit tibi argūmentum semper in prōmptū situm: nē quid expectēs amīcōs, quod tūte agere possiēs
phrases.english: keep this lesson always to hand: don’t wait for your friends to do what you can do yourself

phrases.latin: ut tibi ad mē ōrnandum semper dētur facultās, mihi ad remūnerandum nihil suppetat praeter voluntātem
phrases.english: that you always have the means to do me honour, and I have nothing available to repay you with but goodwill

sources: Lewis & Short: suppeto · Lewis & Short: promptus (in prōmptū) · Lewis & Short: parabilis · Lewis & Short: copia
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. available: easily available; available: make available.

Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-gellius, loci-quintilianus), checked against the editions named there; Terence (Ph. 113), Cicero (Fam. 15.13.2) and Caesar (BG 1.16.2) checked against the Perseus Latin texts.
